It was observed empirically in \cite{MMP-2019-LPCliquesPaley} that $\vartheta(\overline{G_{p,1}}) \sim \sqrt{p/2}$

    $\vartheta(\overline{G_{p,1}}) \sim \sqrt{p/2}$ (for $p \equiv 1 \pmod{4}$ prime) where $G_{p,1}$ is the 1-localization of the Paley Graph described above.
target: For each prime p congruent to 1 modulo 4, let G_p have vertex set F_p, with distinct a,b adjacent exactly when a-b is a nonzero square in F_p, and let H_p be the subgraph induced by the neighbors of 0. Let complement(H_p) use the same localized vertex set. For a finite graph H, define theta(H)=max sum_{u,v} X_{u,v}, over real positive-semidefinite X with trace(X)=1 and X_{u,v}=0 for every edge uv of H. Prove that theta(complement(H_p))/sqrt(p/2) tends to 1 as p tends to infinity through primes congruent to 1 modulo 4, or rigorously prove that this limit is not 1.
title: Lovasz theta of the Paley 1-localization
